'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza–Israel conflict]]
**[[Israel–Hamas war]]
***[[2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip|Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip]]
****The [[United Nations]] says the lives of at least 120 newborn babies in [[incubator (neonatal)|incubator]]s in Gaza hospitals are at risk, as fuel runs out in the enclave. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/10/22/over-100-incubator-babies-at-risk-due-to-israels-fuel-cuts-to-gaza-un (Al Jazeera)]
***[[List of journalists killed in the Israel–Hamas war|Journalists killed in the Israel–Hamas war]]
****[[Palestinians|Palestinian]] journalist Rushdi Sarraj is killed in an [[Israeli Defense Forces|Israeli]] attack on his home. [https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/22/10/2023/palestinian-journalist-killed-by-israeli-attacks-in-gaza (The Peninsula)]
***[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)]]
****Five [[Hezbollah]] members are killed during a [[shootout]] with Israeli soldiers at the border with [[Lebanon]], bringing the number of Hezbollah members killed during the conflict to 24. [https://apnews.com/article/lebanon-israel-hezbollah-gaza-clashes-c279d38d6b67cac526ac95e63f9cca73 (AP)]
***At least 55 Palestinians are killed in overnight [[Israel]]i raids on the Gaza Strip, according to the Hamas-controlled [[Gaza Ministry of Health]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/10/22/israeli-air-raids-kill-at-least-55-in-gaza-overnight-hamas-says (Al Jazeera)]
***The number of [[mosque]]s destroyed by Israeli airstrikes in the Gaza Strip increases to 31. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israel-has-destroyed-31-mosques-in-gaza-strip-since-oct-7-ministry/3029091 (AA)]
***An Israeli tank accidentally hits an [[Egypt]]ian position near the border with Gaza. Several Egyptian [[border guard]]s sustain injuries from [[Shell (projectile)|shell]] fragments. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-military-says-mistakenly-hit-egyptian-position-near-gaza-border-2023-10-22/ (Reuters)]	
***At least 300 Palestinians are placed under [[administrative detention]] or have had detention orders renewed, allowing Israel to [[detention without charge|hold them without charge]] indefinitely under secret evidence. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/10/21/israel-gaza-war-hamas-and-israel-spar-over-hostage-release (Al Jazeera)]	
***[[Paddy Cosgrave]], a co-founder of the European tech conference [[Web Summit]], resigns after opposition to his public statements on Israel, which included, "[[War crime]]s are war crimes even when committed by allies, and should be called out for what they are." [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2023/10/22/web-summit-tech-conference-chief-quits-israel-backlash/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Israel]] launches [[airstrike]]s against [[Damascus International Airport]], killing two workers. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-air-strikes-kill-two-workers-syrias-damascus-airport-official-2023-10-22/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 28 people are killed after a boat capsizes on the [[Congo River]] in [[Province of Équateur|Équateur Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2023/10/23/at-least-28-people-drown-after-boat-capsizes-on-river-in-northwest-congo// (Africa News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war protests]]
**Several thousand people gather in [[Sarajevo]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], waving [[flag of Palestine|Palestinian]] and [[Bosnian flag]]s and demanding an end to Israel's bombardment of [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/thousands-join-pro-palestinian-protest-bosnia-2023-10-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea]]
**The [[Philippines]] reports separate [[Ship collision|collision]] incidents between [[Armed Forces of the Philippines|its military]] ships and vessels of both the [[China Coast Guard]] and the [[Maritime Militia (China)|Maritime Militia]] near the [[Second Thomas Shoal]] in the [[Spratly Islands]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/irresponsible-illegal-actions-philippines-says-china-hit-resupply-boat-4503986 (AFP via NDTV)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Alaska Airlines Flight 2059]]
**An off-duty pilot reportedly attempts to [[Aircraft hijacking|hijack]] and crash an [[Alaska Airlines]] passenger plane travelling from [[Everett, Washington]], to [[San Francisco]], [[California]], [[United States]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-67177294 (BBC News)]
*[[Israel–Hamas war protests]]
**During a pro-Palestine protest in [[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]], U.S., a white car drives through a group of protesters. No one is injured. [https://www.newsweek.com/video-shows-hostile-driver-plow-through-minneapolis-pro-palestinian-rally-1836786 (Newsweek)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Elections in Venezuela]]
**[[2023 Unitary Platform presidential primaries]]
***[[Venezuela]]n [[List of political parties in Venezuela|opposition parties]] hold their first [[Partisan primary|presidential primary]] since 2012. [https://apnews.com/article/venezuela-maduro-opposition-machado-primary-election-072edd20aa8152f3c598f6b68b584df7 (AP)]
*[[2023 Argentine general election]]
**[[Argentines]] elect the [[President of Argentina|president]] and the members of the legislature. [[Sergio Massa]] and [[Javier Milei]] receives ~36% and ~30% of the votes respectively and will face off in a second round. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/argentina-heads-polls-grip-fierce-economic-crisis-2023-10-22/ (Reuters)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/10/22/americas/argentina-vote-president-intl-latam/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2023 Swiss federal election]]
**Voters in [[Switzerland]] elect the members of the [[Federal Assembly (Switzerland)|Federal Assembly]]. Results show that the [[Right-wing politics|right-wing]] [[Swiss People's Party]] becomes the largest [[parliamentary faction]] after the election, gaining nine seats compared to [[2019 Swiss federal election|the previous election]]. [https://apnews.com/article/switzerland-election-final-results-legislative-elections-e677e20c461301d046f249dbebf7c77a (AP)]
*[[2024 Indonesian presidential election]]
**[[Ministry of Defense (Indonesia)|Defense minister]] and [[Gerindra Party|Gerindra]] [[President of Indonesia|presidential]] candidate [[Prabowo Subianto]] chooses [[Surakarta]] mayor [[Gibran Rakabuming Raka]], the eldest child of incumbent president [[Joko Widodo]], as his [[running mate]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/oct/23/indonesia-gibran-rakabuming-raka-son-of-joko-widodo-running-mate-presidential-candidate-prabowo-subianto (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]
